extracted.intended_audience: Prospective NEH applicants: public humanities organizations, museum and library staff, K-12 and higher-education faculty, and media producers
extracted.subtask_short: applying for NEH Lifelong Learning grants
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for developing and proposing projects to the NEH Division of Lifelong Learning, including what types of public humanities, education, and media projects the Division funds and procedural advice for applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop quality humanities programs that foster public engagement and appreciation
rubrics_metrics.description: "By developing quality humanities programs that foster public engagement in and appreciation for the humanities, the Division of Lifelong Learning delivers the best in the humanities for all Americans.",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects should center on quality humanities content and be designed to promote public engagement and appreciation. The Division emphasizes programs that communicate humanities ideas clearly and meaningfully to non-specialist audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reach large and diverse public audiences
rubrics_metrics.description: "The division supports a wide range of public humanities programming that reaches large and diverse public audiences",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funded public humanities projects are expected to reach broad and diverse segments of the public rather than small, closed groups. Proposals should demonstrate audience reach, accessibility, and strategies for engaging diverse populations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use a variety of formats to present humanities work
rubrics_metrics.description: "make use of a variety of formats—interpretation at historic sites, television and radio productions, museum exhibitions, podcasts, short videos, digital games, websites, mobile apps, and other digital media.",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NEH supports multiple presentation media; applicants should choose formats appropriate for their audiences and goals. Proposals should justify format choice, and may combine formats (in-person interpretation, broadcast, digital projects, games, apps, etc.). Examples of previously funded formats are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible project venues and organizational types
rubrics_metrics.description: "The Division supports humanities projects in museums, historical and cultural organizations, libraries, K-12 classrooms, and colleges and universities, as well as for television, radio, and digital media.",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should be or partner with institutions such as museums, cultural organizations, libraries, K–12 schools, colleges/universities, or media producers. Proposals should explain institutional roles and capacity to carry out the project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Humanities Projects: bring humanities ideas to life for general audiences
rubrics_metrics.description: "Public Humanities Projects grants supports projects that bring the ideas of the humanities to life for general audiences through public programming.",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This program funds public programming (exhibitions, lectures, events, community programs, etc.) aimed at helping general audiences understand and engage with humanities ideas. Proposals should articulate how programming will translate humanities content for the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media Projects: development/production/distribution of broadcast and film media
rubrics_metrics.description: "The Media Projects program supports the development, production, and distribution of radio programs, podcasts, long-form documentary films, and documentary film series that engage general audiences with humanities ideas in creative and appealing ways.",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Media proposals should focus on concept development, high-quality production, and distribution strategies that reach broad audiences. Proposers must demonstrate how the media work will interpret humanities ideas and how it will be made accessible to the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Curriculum Development: Western Civilization scope
rubrics_metrics.description: "Supports the development or enhancement of undergraduate and graduate programs, resources, or courses on Western civilization, American history, government, civics, and the Great Books tradition.",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This funding stream is for curricular development in specified subject areas; proposals should describe curricular goals, target student populations (undergraduate/graduate), and how the materials or courses will strengthen teaching and learning in these fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Landmarks and Summer Institutes: national workshops for educators
rubrics_metrics.description: "Landmarks of American History and Culture and Summer Institutes for K-12 Educators: Supports summer workshops for a national audience of K-12 educators that strengthen humanities teaching."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals for Landmarks/Summer Institutes should be organized as summer residential workshops intended for a national cohort of K–12 teachers (or separately for higher-education faculty). They should strengthen classroom teaching of humanities content and include substantive scholarly engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summer Institutes for Higher Education: workshops for faculty and humanities professionals
rubrics_metrics.description: "Landmarks of American History and Culture and Summer Institutes for Higher Education: Supports summer workshops for a national audience of higher education faculty and humanities professionals that strengthen humanities teaching.",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These programs should bring higher-education faculty and humanities professionals together for residential summer workshops that deepen knowledge and provide tools to enhance undergraduate or graduate humanities teaching.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional development programs characteristics (intensive reading and discussion programs)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Intensive reading and discussion programs featuring recognized scholars bring together small communities of teachers at both the higher education and K-12 levels to investigate new themes and innovative approaches to humanities subjects. Largely residential and held during the summer, these programs encourage the study of common texts and other resources, include visits to collections in libraries and museums, and help faculty integrate what has been learned back into their classrooms.",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals for professional development should outline elements such as involvement of recognized scholars, small cohort-based discussion, common-text study, residential/summer scheduling, integrated visits to collections, and explicit plans for participants to integrate learning into their teaching practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for broad institutional efforts to enhance humanities content
rubrics_metrics.description: "The division has several grant programs to support broad institutional efforts to enhance the humanities content of existing programs, develop new programs, or lay the foundation for more extensive endeavors.",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NEH will fund institution-level initiatives that strengthen or expand humanities offerings. Proposals should describe institutional scope, sustainability, and how the project will build capacity or serve as a foundation for larger initiatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for integrative collaborative curricular projects across disciplines
rubrics_metrics.description: "The division also supports creative, integrative, collaborative curricular projects at two- and four-year post-secondary institutions between the humanities, and STEM, pre-professional, and professional programs in law, the health sciences, etc.",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects that build cross-disciplinary curricula (humanities + STEM, pre-professional or professional programs) are encouraged. Proposals should demonstrate meaningful integration of humanities perspectives with other disciplines, collaboration across departments, and relevance to student learning or career preparation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program officer assistance and proposal-preparation guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: "Program officers are prepared to answer a wide variety of questions from prospective applicants. They can provide information about the division’s application guidelines and the eligibility or competitiveness of potential project ideas, and provide tips about common proposal-writing mistakes to avoid. They will supply samples of successful application narratives in each grant category and even provide feedback for a preliminary draft of a proposal if it is submitted well before the deadline. All potential applicants are encouraged to contact a program officer early in their project conceptualization process.",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should contact a program officer early for guidance on eligibility, competitiveness, common proposal-writing mistakes, and to request sample successful narratives. Draft proposals submitted well before the deadline may receive feedback; use this resource to strengthen applications and confirm fit with program goals.
